question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Madras — Location & Foundation]
options: Madras (Chennai) is located on the Coromandel Coast on the eastern coast of India
Fort St. George was built by the English at Madras in 1639–1640
Madras lies on the shores of the Bay of Bengal
Madras was founded by the English on land purchased from the Dutch East India Company
wrong_fact: Madras was NOT founded on land purchased from the Dutch. Francis Day of the English East India Company obtained a strip of land from the local Nayak ruler (Damarla Venkatadri Nayak, acting for the Vijayanagara successor state) in 1639. Fort St. George was then constructed in 1640. The Dutch had no role in granting this land.
explanation: Madras (modern Chennai) lies on the Coromandel Coast facing the Bay of Bengal. Francis Day negotiated a lease of land from the Nayak of Wandiwash in 1639, and Francis Day along with Andrew Cogan built Fort St. George — the first English fort in India — by 1640. This became the nucleus of the Madras Presidency. The Dutch were rivals, not land-grantors.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Madras — Geographical Setting & Hinterland]
options: Madras serves as a gateway to the Deccan and South Indian hinterland via the Eastern Ghats passes
The Cooum and Adyar rivers flow through the Madras/Chennai urban area
The Pulicat Lake, a lagoon north of Madras, was once the site of the main Dutch settlement on the Coromandel Coast
Madras is situated at the delta of the Cauvery River, making it a natural inland waterway hub
wrong_fact: Madras is NOT situated at the Cauvery delta. The Cauvery delta lies much further south, centred on Thanjavur and emptying into the sea near Nagapattinam/Poompuhar — about 300 km south of Madras. Madras is a coastal city between the smaller Cooum and Adyar rivers, and had no natural river delta to serve as an inland waterway hub.
explanation: The Cooum and Adyar rivers bracket the city of Madras. Pulicat Lake (to the north) was the headquarters of the Dutch on the Coromandel Coast (Geldria fort). Access to the Deccan was via passes through the Eastern Ghats. The Cauvery delta system is centred on Thanjavur/Kumbakonam, far south of Madras.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Madras — Battle of Wandiwash & French Rivalry]
options: The Battle of Wandiwash (1760) was fought about 100 km south-west of Madras in present-day Tamil Nadu
The English General Sir Eyre Coote defeated the French General Comte de Lally at Wandiwash
After the fall of Pondicherry (1761) following Wandiwash, French power in India effectively ended
The Battle of Wandiwash was fought near the coast of the Bay of Bengal, with naval support deciding the outcome
wrong_fact: The Battle of Wandiwash was NOT a coastal battle decided by naval support. It was an inland engagement near Wandiwash town (Tamil Nadu), fought between English and French land armies. Naval power was irrelevant at this inland site. The decisive factor was Eyre Coote's superior tactics and the capture of Marquis de Bussy.
explanation: Wandiwash (Vandavasi) is an inland town in the Ranipet district of Tamil Nadu, roughly 100–130 km south-west of Madras. On 22 January 1760, Eyre Coote decisively defeated Comte de Lally and captured the Marquis de Bussy. This land battle, combined with the English naval blockade, led to the surrender of Pondicherry in 1761, ending French territorial ambitions in India.
